text.p: The deadline for arbitration of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) dispute with India's state-owned National Housing Bank (NHB) has been extended to the end of March, chief Don Mercer told Reuters.
"The latest we've heard is that the deadline has been extended to the end of March," Mercer told Reuters here.

The NHB has made claims against ANZ and the dispute has been subject to an arbitration process since the beginning of 1993. The claim relates to a US$1.2 billion banking scandal in 1992. ANZ paid the equivalent of A$250 million to the Indian bank, pending arbitration.
Mercer said ANZ was very positive about India, where it has 56 branches and where it has been operating since the mid-19th century.
He said ANZ was looking to expansion elsewhere in Asia, particularly in Indonesia and the Philippines where it had only single branches.
ANZ has applied for a licence to open a second branch in China in Beijing, Mercer said. It has a branch in Shanghai. "We are very hopeful our application will be considered favourably," he said.
